shared_elements: shallow low-relief carving on coarse stone
animal in profile with arched back and downturned head
elongated tapering forms suggesting limbs or beaks
irregular natural block edge left uncarved
justification: Both surfaces share the same basic idiom of shallow, rounded low relief in coarse stone, and in each a profile creature with an arched back and a long tapering head or beak dominates the carved field, with a broad curved arc arching above it. But B is a tall, deliberately shaped pillar organised into stacked horizontal registers with a patterned band and multiple discrete figures, while A is a single low, irregular boulder face with one weathered, ambiguous composition and no register scheme, so the correspondence remains generic rather than compositional.
